segments: to Antioch.
Because of the oaths, that is to say, which he swore to them,
he sent Turks against them on the road, and they killed them.
And during this journey,
the treasure of our church in Mar'ash was lost at the hands of the priests who had rebelled against the bishop:
a flask of chrism,
and cups, and phials,
and silver censers,
and vestments, and veils.
And the lord of Hisn Ziyad,
who was Qara Arslan,
took Babula from the Franks,
and sent raiding bands to the territory of Gargar.
And when they saw
that all the people and their families were sheltered in the mountains of Mar Bar Sawma,
they set ambushes in three places;
and in the morning they attacked and carried off the flocks and the cattle.
And three of the monastery's dependents were killed,
and two of the Turks.
And the Turks sent word to the monastery:
"Surrender the people of Gargar to us,
so that we may return to you everything that {OCR?} we took as booty.
For we honor this holy man,
and we make vows to him,
and it was not to do evil in his monastery that we came.
When we take the people,
it is not into slavery that we are leading them,
but to bring them and settle them in their villages,
that they may be cultivators for us."
And dissension fell upon the monastery:
some of them were saying,
"We will give them up,"
and some of them,
"No,"
until the monks were close to falling upon one another with the sword.
Then an old monk
took two individuals from both sides,
and they went out to the Turks, and he said (or: they said) to them:
"If you speak in truth,
and it is for cultivation and not for slavery that you seek these people,
let some men among you come with us, that we may go to your protected {OCR?} emir,
and whatever he commands in his justice, we will do."
Then their deceit was exposed.
And the monks agreed among themselves,
and all of them cried out with one voice,
"We will not give them up!"
The Turks then burned the winepresses and the fences of the vineyards,
and they left and went away.
And the monks went to Hisn Ziyad,
and appeared before the emir.
And God placed mercy in his heart,
and he returned all the captives and booty.
And in that same year,
when Joscelin set out from Tell Bashir to go to Antioch with two hundred horsemen,
those who thought that they could face a thousand,
while marching by night,
a few Turkmen encountered them,
and from the mere sound, they took fright and fled.
And the Turks pursued after them,
